fact_sheet.business_description: the Company operates major rental brands across North America and international markets, combining airport and local distribution, fleet procurement, maintenance, and vehicle disposal [D01]. The business depends on rental volume, utilization, and depreciation management rather than being a simple rental-rate spread model [D01].
segments_and_mix: Americas: Revenue $2.062 billion, adjusted segment EBITDA $(169) million [D01]
International: Revenue $514 million, adjusted EBITDA $63 million [D01]
unit_economics: Monthly depreciation per unit was $537, up from $284 year-over-year [D01]
Utilization was 82%; transaction days were 41.298 million in Q3 [D01]
Adjusted free cash flow was negative $154 million [D02]
Management targets normalized monthly depreciation under $300 by end-2025 [D03]
competitive_position: Industry is a concentrated oligopoly consisting of Enterprise (private), Avis Budget, and the Company [D06]
Major assets include brand recognition and airport access, but vehicles are not a perpetual intangible franchise [D01]
Competitive performance is evidenced by Avis Budget remaining EBITDA positive in Q3 2024 while the Company was negative [D06]

Adjusted Corporate EBITDA declined from $561 million in 2023 to $(157) million in Q3 2024 [D02, D03]
Transformation and fleet rotation expected to be substantially complete by end-2025 [D03]

Corporate liquidity was $1.6 billion as of September 30 [D02, D03]
Includes $1 billion in June 2024 financing (senior secured and PIK notes) [D07]

management_governance.evidence: CEO Gil West was appointed in 2024 to implement a 'back-to-basics' turnaround strategy, providing a clear path for potential improvement [D01, D03].

durable_growth_runway.evidence: Future growth remains speculative until the company successfully completes its fleet rotation and stabilizes EBITDA, which is expected by end-2025 [D03].

We believe the equity serves as a levered call option on management's ability to normalize monthly depreciation to under $300 and stabilize EBITDA by end-2025, supported by current liquidity of $1.6 billion [D03, D07].

Since a new CEO is already implementing a coherent plan that we agree with, we prefer to monitor execution and allow the market to re-rate the business as operational metrics normalize, rather than engaging publicly or seeking control [D03].

final.memo:
The Company operates a major rental brand network that, while currently facing severe operational headwinds, maintains critical competitive advantages through its airport infrastructure and scale within a concentrated oligopoly [D01, D06]. Under the leadership of CEO Gil West, who joined in 2024, the business has initiated a necessary 'back-to-basics' turnaround and comprehensive fleet rotation [D01, D03].

The current opportunity exists because the market has priced the equity for a distressed scenario, fixated on recent negative EBITDA and $1 billion in impairment charges [D03, D05, D06]. We believe the market misjudges the company's ability to bridge this transition, as the $1.6 billion in current liquidity provides sufficient runway to complete the restructuring by the end of 2025 [D02, D03, D07].

While traditional valuation metrics like P/E are currently non-meaningful due to operating losses, the path to value recovery is clear: normalizing monthly depreciation per unit from $537 down to below $300 [D01, D03, D04]. Achieving this alongside a return to historical EBITDA margins of 10-12% implies an attractive, albeit speculative, internal rate of return exceeding 25% if the turnaround succeeds [D03].

Our role is that of a passive observer; we believe the management team has identified the correct operational levers to restore the business and we intend to monitor the execution of the fleet rotation quietly [D03]. The primary risks involve the company's high leverage and sensitivity to residual value fluctuations in the used-car market, which could result in permanent loss of capital if the turnaround stalls [D02, D03, D05, D06].

Given the speculative nature of this investment, we are initiating a small position of 2% of NAV [D02, D03]. This sizing reflects the high risk-reward profile of this turnaround while ensuring our exposure remains bounded should the operational execution fall short of our targets [D03, D05].
